title: Wear-IT Study Specification
description: This specification contains all the needed information to both run a study using the Wear-IT framework. This includes all the needed information to make reproducible and replicable codebooks for complex designs.

examples.Study.Name: Recovery Community Center Project
examples.authors: Jane Smith, John Doe, Emily R. Johnson
examples.abstract: This study examined daily stress and recovery patterns among adults attending a recovery community center. Participants completed ecological momentary assessments four times daily over 14 days across two bursts.

Study.Name.description: Human readable long name for a study

authors.description: String of all people to be credited for this study. This will appear in the authors section of a generated codebook.

funding.description: String containing relevant funding info for the study

abstract.description: String containing qualitative description of the study. This could include main study objectives, relevant findings, study population etc.

burst.title: Burst Specification
burst.description: Contains all the information to specify burst design

Timing.Type.description: Type of timing. Discrete means equal time distance, random, is drawing a random sample from a time period, triggered is based on set rules more in depth than just random in a time period, and continous is uneven time intervals.

survey.title: Survey Specification
survey.description: Contains all the information needed to specify survey design

Scheduling.Info.description: Contains all the timing and window info for a survey

offset.description: Distance between each survey at this level

Window.Info.description: Contains all the window info for a survey

window.length.description: Describes the length of a window.

random.description: Whether the delivery of a survey is a random sample within the window

Trigger.Info.description: Contains the trigger logic if it exists for a given window.

Conditional.Source.description: Source of measurement to trigger conditional

Conditional.Threshold.description: Threshold is the preset value being compared to the user response.

Conditional.Type.description: Conditional type is the comparator (in order: =, <=, >=, <, >, !=)

question.title: Question Specification
question.description: Contains all the information needed to specify a question or variable in a survey, observation, or passive data collection context.

examples.Question.Long.Name: Perceived Stress Item 1
examples.Question.Text: How stressed have you felt in the past hour?
examples.Question.Description: A self-report measure of perceived stress on a scale from 0 (not at all) to 100 (extremely).
examples.Question.Type.Display.Name: Slider

Question.ID.description: Name of the variable as it appears in the dataset

Question.Long.Name.description: Human readable name for the variable

Question.Text.description: Exact text of the question as presented to the participant. Only applicable for survey questions.

Question.Description.description: Description of the variable in layman's terms. If layman's terms are not possible, provide a citation to a longer explanation.

Question.Type.Display.Name.description: How the data was obtained. Must match one of the supported Wear-IT display types.

descriptions.Free Response: Open-ended free text response from the participant.
descriptions.Informational Fullscreen: Displays information to the participant only — no user response is collected.
descriptions.Multiple Choice: Participant selects exactly one option from a list of choices.
descriptions.Multiple Select: Participant selects one or more options from a list of choices.
descriptions.Multiple Slider: Multiple visual analog scales presented together, one per construct.
descriptions.Slider: A single visual analog scale — participant drags to a position between two anchors.
descriptions.Time Picker: A time-based analog of the slider — participant selects a time value rather than a numeric one.

examples.definition: Less than five minutes (just stopped in)

definition.description: Human-readable label for the response value.

Parent.description: Item ID of the parent item. NOTE: This is different than the conditional master which points to the item which if successful, delivers the current. Parent may point to a block many questions up.

Conditional.Info.description: Contains all the conditional info for a question

Conditional.Child.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the successful child of the current question.

Conditional.Fail.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the fail child of the current question.

Conditional.Master.Item.ID.description: Item ID for the parent of the current question.

Conditional.Threshold.description: Threshold is the preset value being compared to the user response.

Conditional.Type.description: Conditional type is the comparator (in order: =, <=, >=, <, >, !=)

Data.Type.description: The type of data captured by this variable. Oldname: Result.Type

data.title: Data Specification (Column Vector Format)
data.description: All fields are stored as column vectors (arrays), where each position corresponds to a participant/record in the dataset.

Alert.Times.description: Each entry is a participant-level array of alert times.

itemMap.title: Item Map Repo
itemMap.description: This specification contains all the needed information to describe a single item or scale used within the Wear-IT framework, including its conceptual, psychometric, and delivery properties.

examples.Item.Text: How stressed did you feel today?
examples.Modeling.Characteristics: Typically used as an outcome variable; no transformation required
examples.Scale.Name: Perceived Stress Scale
examples.Top.Level.Question: Indicate to what extent you...
examples.Definition: Never, Almost Never, Sometimes, Fairly Often, Very Often
examples.Article.Title: A global measure of perceived stress
examples.Citation: Cohen, S., Kamarck, T., & Mermelstein, R. (1983). https://doi.org/10.2307/2136404
examples.notes: Standard PSS-10 item; time stem adapted from original

Item.Text.description: Exact text of the item as presented.

Conceptualization.description: What construct or concept does this item measure or represent?

Modeling.Characteristics.description: Usual modeling characteristics or how this item is typically used in analysis (e.g. predictor, outcome, mediator, covariate). For example, reaction time is often log transformed.

Validated.description: Whether this item is part of a statistically validated measure.

Scale.Name.description: Name of the scale this item belongs to.

Parent.Scale.description: Name of the parent scale if this item belongs to a subscale.

Sub.Scale.description: Name of the subscale this item belongs to, if applicable.

scaleOrItem.description: Whether this entry represents a full scale or a single item.

Scale.Type.description: The type of scale this item uses (e.g. Likert, VAS, semantic differential, binary, forced choice).

Scoring.description: How this item or scale is scored, including any summing, averaging, or weighting rules (e.g. sum score, factor scores, weighted sum scores).

Reverse.Coded.description: Whether this item is reverse coded or otherwise transformed before use.

Transformation.description: Description of any transformation applied to this item beyond simple reverse coding. This could also include transformation needed for this item (ie. log-transform reaction time).

Identifying.Info.description: Whether this item potentially contains personally identifying information.

Data.Type.description: Type of data this item produces.

Time.Stem.description: The time reference embedded in the item (e.g. 'in the past week', 'right now', 'today'). This should be the time stem in the cited paper, but can be swapped out to any timestem.

Top.Level.Question.description: The top-level or parent question this item falls under, if it is a sub-item (i.e. Indicate to what extent you...).

Definition.description: Nominal or text-based response options or categories (very slightly or not at all, a little, moderately, quite a bit, extremely).

Delivery.Mechanism.description: How the item is delivered to the participant (e.g. mobile app, paper, wearable, passive sensor, interviewer).

Delivery.Frequency.description: How frequently this item is delivered (e.g. once daily, every 4 hours, event-contingent).

Citation.description: DOI citation for the item or scale source, or APA formatted citation.

notes.description: Any additional notes about this item.
